ai.headline: Anthropic Fable 5 Ban: 100+ Security Experts Sign Open Letter, Negotiations Ongoing
ai.body: Trump administration restricted Fable 5 to US-only after Amazon reportedly demonstrated jailbreaks, forcing Anthropic to pull global access with a 90-minute deadline and no specifics on the threat. Over 100 cybersecurity leaders (Adobe, Zoom, Sophos, Nvidia, Stanford HAI) signed a 'Free Fable' open letter arguing the ban handcuffs defenders while GPT-5.5, Kimi 2.7, and Opus carry equivalent capabilities. Anthropic is now suing DoD over a separate supply-chain-risk designation and dispatching senior staff to DC to negotiate reinstatement.

ai.headline: Open-Weight MoE Models: Architectural Convergence and Cross-Team Innovation
ai.body: ByteByteGo's deep dive shows all frontier open-weight models (DeepSeek V3, Kimi K2, Qwen3, Llama 4, GLM-5) share an MoE skeleton where total vs. active parameters are distinct cost axes — Kimi K2 has 1T total but only 32B active, comparable per-query cost to Qwen3's 22B active. Key divergence points are attention strategy (GQA vs. MLA vs. sparse), expert count (16–384), and post-training recipe (RL, distillation, synthetic agentic data). Public technical reports enable a form of compounding cross-org collaboration with each successive release.

ai.headline: Agentic Code Review Quality Crisis: 861% Churn, 54% Defect Rate
ai.body: Faros AI's 22,000-developer study found AI-assisted coding drove code churn up 861%, per-developer defect rate from 9% to 54%, review duration up 441%, and zero-review merges up 31%. GitClear data shows a 4x raw output gain translates to only ~12% delivered-value gain — the gap is the review bottleneck. The hard centre of engineering has shifted from writing code to deciding whether to trust AI-generated code.

ai.headline: DFlash + SGLang Spec V2: Next-Generation Speculative Decoding Throughput Gains
ai.body: LMSYS published benchmarks for DFlash and SGLang's Spec V2 engine showing substantial throughput improvements over baseline inference and native MTP speculation. This is directly relevant to inference cost optimisation for teams running self-hosted LLM infrastructure.

ai.headline: Dropbox Uses MCP + Dash for Agentic Threat-Model-to-Code Security Gap Closure
ai.body: Dropbox engineering built an agentic review pipeline pairing Dash (threat model indexer), MCP (agent access layer), and a foundation model that diffs the threat model against each PR to surface security gaps inline in code review. This is a concrete production architecture for AI-assisted security review relevant to any team maintaining threat models.

sec.headline: CVE-2026-42824: M365 Copilot SearchLeak — One-Click Data Exfiltration via Prompt Injection
sec.body: Varonis found a three-stage chain in M365 Copilot Enterprise Search: the `q` URL parameter is treated as an instruction, allowing Copilot to be tricked into searching a victim's email, calendar, SharePoint, and OneDrive. Results are embedded in an image URL that briefly renders before sanitization, triggering a request to an attacker-controlled Bing image endpoint with the exfiltrated data. Microsoft patched as CVE-2026-42824; demonstrates how AI-powered search converts legacy web injection bugs into practical exfil paths.

sec.headline: LiteLLM Privilege Escalation Chain: Low-Privilege User → AI Gateway Full Takeover
sec.body: A bug chain in LiteLLM proxy lets a basic internal user mint overbroad API keys, self-escalate to proxy admin, then execute arbitrary Python via guardrail callback hooks for full server takeover, including decrypting stored credentials and reading all prompts/responses. Callback hooks also allow silent response tampering and reverse shell spawning. Fix: upgrade to v1.83.14-stable, audit admin/callback configs, and rotate all exposed AI provider keys.

sec.headline: Humanity Protocol $36M Hack: Phishing Email → Private Key Theft → Dual-Chain Proxy Hijack
sec.body: A single spear-phishing email to director Chong Yee Wai (impersonating Bithumb exchange) delivered RAT malware that extracted private keys controlling Hyperlane warp-route proxies and three BSC Safe signer keys. The attacker simultaneously replaced the proxy implementation on Ethereum to redirect ~141M $H tokens and used stolen BSC signers to seize ProxyAdmin and mint 100M additional tokens, conducting both chains in parallel to prevent defensive response. $H crashed 89%; proceeds liquidated via Uniswap/PancakeSwap over ~8 hours — underscores that admin key holders need HSMs, geographically-separated multisig ceremonies, and air-gapped signing devices.

sec.headline: ShinyHunters Claims Council of Europe Breach: 429K Files Including Payroll, Bank Accounts, Medical Records
sec.body: ShinyHunters claims to have exfiltrated 429K files from the Council of Europe including employee payroll, bank account data, medical records, CVs, and performance evaluations. The same group separately leaked 137K school staff accounts from InfiniteCampus's Salesforce instance, verified by Have I Been Pwned. ShinyHunters continues targeting institutional and SaaS-hosted data at scale.

sec.headline: VS Code Extension Supply Chain: CDN URL Bypass Makes Marketplace Blocks Ineffective
sec.body: Post-mortem on the VS Code supply chain attack reveals many orgs only blocked marketplace.visualstudio.com but not the CDN URLs that actually serve extension packages — attackers knowing or reconstructing CDN URLs can bypass controls entirely. Direct extraction into .vscode/extensions/ also bypasses install-time restrictions. Effective mitigations require blocking CDN endpoints and enforcing extension allowlists at the filesystem level.

swe.headline: LinkedIn Job Offer Backdoor: Fake Recruiter Delivers Malware via Malicious GitHub Repo Code Review
swe.body: A developer received a LinkedIn recruiter message requesting a 'code review' of a GitHub repository; sandbox analysis revealed the repo contained a backdoor delivering malware on execution. This social engineering vector is specifically targeting developers by exploiting normal professional workflows (code review requests). Teams should enforce sandboxed environments for all third-party code evaluation and treat unsolicited repository access requests as high-risk.

swe.headline: TimescaleDB Hypercore: Up to 98% Compression for Time-Series Data in PostgreSQL
swe.body: TimescaleDB's Hypercore engine uses a hybrid row-columnar model with delta encoding, Gorilla XOR, and run-length encoding to achieve up to 98% compression ratios on time-series data. Data must be partitioned to enable batching of ~1,000 rows for the compression algorithms to exploit cross-row patterns. Relevant for fintech teams storing high-volume event/transaction time-series in Postgres.

mkt.headline: Fox Acquires Roku for ~$25B; Combined Entity to Compete with Amazon and Netflix for Ad Dollars
mkt.body: Fox is buying Roku in a ~$25B deal expected to close H1 2027, adding streaming scale to Fox One and Fox Nation subscription tiers. The combined company is positioned to compete directly with Amazon and Netflix for connected-TV ad spend. Relevant for AMZN holders monitoring the streaming/CTV competitive landscape.

mkt.headline: Market Rally: Nasdaq +3.07%, Dow New Record, SpaceX +19.6% Post-Debut; Oil Falls on Iran Deal
mkt.body: Wall Street posted strong gains on 2026-06-16 — Nasdaq best day since end of March, Dow hit a new all-time record — driven by falling oil prices after a preliminary US-Iran peace deal sent crude lower and retail gas below $4. SpaceX surged 19.6% in continued post-IPO momentum. Positive macro read for tech portfolio holdings (MSFT, GOOGL, AMZN, NVDA).
